The act of State doctrine generally bars a court from adjudicating the validity of a foreign sovereign's official acts taken within its own territory, based on comity and sovereign equality. Of the two options given, the better fit is that the courts are well placed to assess an alleged tort committed by the State unless there are strong reasons otherwise—though this phrasing is imprecise, since the doctrine typically counsels abstention rather than confidence in judicial assessment. The option that "all State acts attract immunity" is too broad, as the doctrine is distinct from immunity and does not cover every act.

CONFIDENCE: 60
